cards.explanation: The answer is False. The wives join in, and so do the sons and daughters who are able to understand (Nehemiah 10:28). That's the qualification, friends: the children who can understand are the ones included. I love a full kitchen, and this is a full kitchen.

The answer is to follow the Law of God given through Moses. The people commit "…with a sworn oath to follow the Law of God given through His servant Moses and to obey carefully all the commandments, ordinances, and statutes of the LORD our Lord." (Nehemiah 10:29). Moses, Israel's leader, is the one the Law came through. Everything else in the oath hangs on this promise, friends, like every cookie in my bakery hangs on the recipe.

The word is "marry." The words are "We will not give our daughters in marriage to the people of the land, and we will not take their daughters for our sons." (Nehemiah 10:30). Marriage is the promise, friends, and it goes both ways, daughters and sons. Simple as a two-ingredient dough.

The answer is that they won't buy from them that day. The promise is that they "…will not buy from them on a Sabbath or holy day." (Nehemiah 10:31). Not even a little, friends. When the oven is off for the day, the oven is OFF, and no sale changes that.

The answer is True. The verse says "Every seventh year we will let the fields lie fallow and will cancel every debt." (Nehemiah 10:31). Both promises sit in the same sentence, so the fields rest and the debts get canceled in that seventh year. Rest for the land, and a clean slate for the folks owing money. I'd sign that, friends.

The big promise is that they won't neglect the house of their God. The oath ends with "Thus we will not neglect the house of our God." (Nehemiah 10:39). All those gifts, the grain, the wine and the oil, back up that one promise, friends. I think of it like keeping the bakery lights on, and that takes steady work, not one big day.
